body.en: Quadratic and polynomial functions constitute approximately 15% of the EST I Mathematics exam (tested across both Section I No-Calculator and Section II Calculator). High-scoring students must fluidly convert between standard, vertex, and factored forms, leverage the discriminant \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\) to classify real versus complex roots, exploit Vieta's formulas for sum and product of roots, and apply the Polynomial Remainder and Factor Theorems.
body.ar: Quadratic and كثيرة الحدود الدوال constitute approximately 15% of the EST I Mathematics exam (tested across both Section I No-Calculator and Section II Calculator). High-scoring students must fluidly convert between standard, الرأس, and factored forms, leverage the discriminant \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\) to classify real versus complex roots, exploit Vieta's الصيغ for sum and product of roots, and apply the كثيرة الحدود Remainder and Factor Theorems.

label.en: Definition 2.1 — Quadratic Forms, Parabola Anatomy, and Vieta's Relations
label.ar: تعريف 2.1 — Quadratic Forms, القطع المكافئ Anatomy, and Vieta's Relations

body.en:
Essential algebraic forms and fundamental properties of quadratic functions:
  • Standard Form: \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) with \(a \neq 0\).
    The \(y\)-intercept is \((0, c)\). The vertical axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\). If \(a > 0\), the parabola opens upward (minimum value at vertex); if \(a < 0\), it opens downward (maximum value at vertex).
  • Vertex Form: \(f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k\), where \((h, k)\) is the vertex.
    The extreme value of the function is \(f(h) = k\). Converting from standard form uses completing the square or \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\) with \(k = f(h)\).
  • Factored (Intercept) Form: \(f(x) = a(x - r_1)(x - r_2)\), where \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) are the \(x\)-intercepts (roots/zeros). The axis of symmetry lies at the midpoint: \(h = \frac{r_1 + r_2}{2}\).
  • Vieta's Relations for Quadratics: For any quadratic equation \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) with roots \(r_1\) and \(r_2\):
    \[ r_1 + r_2 = -\frac{b}{a}, \qquad r_1 r_2 = \frac{c}{a} \]
body.ar:
Essential algebraic forms and fundamental properties of quadratic الدوال:
  • Standard Form: \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) with \(a \neq 0\).
    The \(y\)-المقطع is \((0, c)\). The vertical axis of symmetry is \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\). If \(a > 0\), the القطع المكافئ opens upward (minimum value at الرأس); if \(a < 0\), it opens downward (maximum value at الرأس).
  • Vertex Form: \(f(x) = a(x - h)^2 + k\), حيث \((h, k)\) is the الرأس.
    The extreme value of the الدالة is \(f(h) = k\). Converting from standard form uses completing the square or \(h = -\frac{b}{2a}\) with \(k = f(h)\).
  • Factored (المقطع) Form: \(f(x) = a(x - r_1)(x - r_2)\), حيث \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) are the \(x\)-intercepts (roots/zeros). The axis of symmetry lies at the midpoint: \(h = \frac{r_1 + r_2}{2}\).
  • Vieta's Relations for Quadratics: For any المعادلة التربيعية \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) with roots \(r_1\) and \(r_2\):
    \[ r_1 + r_2 = -\frac{b}{a}, \qquad r_1 r_2 = \frac{c}{a} \]

body.en: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental function \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical equations, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the solution set, requiring a final domain check against the original equation.
body.ar: Domain Restrictions, Invertibility & Asymptotic Behavior: An algebraic or transcendental الدالة \(f: D \to R\) possesses an inverse \(f^{-1}: R \to D\) if and only if \(f\) is strictly one-to-one (bijective) on \(D\), guaranteeing that \(\text{dom}(f^{-1}) = \text{ran}(f)\) and \(\text{ran}(f^{-1}) = \text{dom}(f)\). For logarithmic and radical المعادلات, every algebraic step that squares both sides or combines logs (\(\log_b u + \log_b v = \log_b(uv)\)) can enlarge the الحل set, requiring a final المجال check against the original المعادلة.

label.en: Theorem 2.1 — The Quadratic Formula, Discriminant Classification, and Remainder Theorem
label.ar: مبرهنة 2.1 — The Quadratic الصيغة, Discriminant Classification, and Remainder مبرهنة

body.en:
Fundamental algebraic criteria for quadratic solutions and polynomial factors:
  • The Quadratic Formula: For any \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) with \(a \neq 0\):
    \[ x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \]
  • Discriminant Root Classification (\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\)):
    1. \(\Delta > 0\): Exactly two distinct real roots (parabola crosses the \(x\)-axis at two points). If \(\Delta\) is a rational perfect square and \(a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q}\), both roots are rational.
    2. \(\Delta = 0\): Exactly one real root of multiplicity 2 (parabola is tangent to the \(x\)-axis at its vertex \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\)).
    3. \(\Delta < 0\): No real roots; exactly two complex conjugate roots \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} \pm i\frac{\sqrt{|\Delta|}}{2a}\) (parabola never intersects the \(x\)-axis).
  • Polynomial Remainder & Factor Theorems:
    Let \(P(x)\) be any polynomial of degree \(n \ge 1\).
    1. Remainder Theorem: When \(P(x)\) is divided by the linear divisor \((x - c)\), the remainder is \(R = P(c)\).
    2. Factor Theorem: A linear binomial \((x - c)\) is a factor of \(P(x) \iff P(c) = 0\).
body.ar:
Fundamental algebraic criteria for quadratic الحلول and كثيرة الحدود factors:
  • The Quadratic الصيغة: For any \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\) with \(a \neq 0\):
    \[ x = \frac{-b \pm \sqrt{b^2 - 4ac}}{2a} \]
  • Discriminant Root Classification (\(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\)):
    1. \(\Delta > 0\): Exactly two distinct real roots (القطع المكافئ crosses the \(x\)-axis at two points). If \(\Delta\) is a rational perfect square and \(a, b, c \in \mathbb{Q}\), both roots are rational.
    2. \(\Delta = 0\): Exactly one real root of multiplicity 2 (القطع المكافئ is tangent to the \(x\)-axis at its الرأس \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\)).
    3. \(\Delta < 0\): No real roots; exactly two complex conjugate roots \(x = -\frac{b}{2a} \pm i\frac{\sqrt{|\Delta|}}{2a}\) (القطع المكافئ never intersects the \(x\)-axis).
  • Polynomial Remainder & Factor Theorems:
    Let \(P(x)\) be any كثيرة الحدود of degree \(n \ge 1\).
    1. Remainder مبرهنة: عندما \(P(x)\) is divided by the linear divisor \((x - c)\), the remainder is \(R = P(c)\).
    2. Factor مبرهنة: A linear binomial \((x - c)\) is a factor of \(P(x) \iff P(c) = 0\).

label.en: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Quadratics & Polynomials
label.ar: ▲ EST I Math Traps & Pitfalls — Quadratics & Polynomials (المعادلات التربيعية وكثيرات الحدود)

body.en:
• Vertex Coordinate Signs: In vertex form \(y = a(x - h)^2 + k\), the vertex is \((h, k)\). Notice the minus sign on \(h\): \(y = 2(x + 3)^2 - 5\) has vertex at \((-3, -5)\), NOT \((3, -5)\). From standard form, \(h = -b/(2a)\).
  • Cancelling Variables Loses Roots: In an equation like \(x^2 = 6x\), NEVER divide both sides by \(x\)! Doing so loses the root \(x = 0\). Instead, set to zero: \(x^2 - 6x = 0 \implies x(x - 6) = 0\), yielding both \(x = 0\) and \(x = 6\).
  • Discriminant Root Classifications: \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\). If \(\Delta > 0\), two distinct real solutions; if \(\Delta = 0\), exactly one real solution; if \(\Delta < 0\), no real solutions (two complex conjugate roots).
  • Sum and Product of Roots (Vieta's Formulas): For \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), root sum is \(r_1 + r_2 = -b/a\) and root product is \(r_1 r_2 = c/a\). This avoids having to solve the equation when the question only asks for the sum or product of solutions.
  • Difference of Squares vs. Sum of Squares: \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\), whereas over the reals \(a^2 + b^2\) is prime (or \((a - bi)(a + bi)\) over the complex numbers).
body.ar:
• Vertex الإحداثي Signs: In الرأس form \(y = a(x - h)^2 + k\), the الرأس is \((h, k)\). Notice the minus sign on \(h\): \(y = 2(x + 3)^2 - 5\) has الرأس at \((-3, -5)\), NOT \((3, -5)\). From standard form, \(h = -b/(2a)\).
  • Cancelling المتغيرات Loses Roots: In an المعادلة like \(x^2 = 6x\), NEVER divide both sides by \(x\)! Doing so loses the root \(x = 0\). Instead, set to zero: \(x^2 - 6x = 0 \implies x(x - 6) = 0\), yielding both \(x = 0\) and \(x = 6\).
  • Discriminant Root Classifications: \(\Delta = b^2 - 4ac\). If \(\Delta > 0\), two distinct real الحلول; if \(\Delta = 0\), exactly one real الحل; if \(\Delta < 0\), no real الحلول (two complex conjugate roots).
  • Sum and Product of Roots (Vieta's الصيغ): For \(ax^2 + bx + c = 0\), root sum is \(r_1 + r_2 = -b/a\) and root product is \(r_1 r_2 = c/a\). This avoids having to حل المعادلة عندما the question only asks for the sum or product of الحلول.
  • Difference of Squares vs. Sum of Squares: \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\), whereas over the reals \(a^2 + b^2\) is prime (or \((a - bi)(a + bi)\) over the complex numbers).

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Quadratics & Polynomials)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (Quadratics & Polynomials)

body.en:
Why Completing the Square & Log-Linearization Work: Any quadratic \(f(x) = ax^2 + bx + c\) (\(a \ne 0\)) can be rewritten by factoring \(a\) from the first two terms and adding/subtracting \((b/2a)^2\):

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the range to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

\[ ax^2 + bx + c = a\!\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 + \left(c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\right) \]

Because \(\left(x + \frac{b}{2a}\right)^2 \ge 0\) for all \(x \in \mathbb{R}\), the extreme value \(k = c - \frac{b^2}{4a}\) is attained uniquely at the axis of symmetry \(x = -\frac{b}{2a}\), restricting the المدى to \([k, \infty)\) (if \(a > 0\)) and making \(f\) invertible on \(x \ge -\frac{b}{2a}\). Similarly, applying \(\ln\) to power laws \(y = ax^n\) yields \(\ln y = n\ln x + \ln a\), transforming a nonlinear curve into a straight line of gradient \(n\).

label.en: Worked Example 2.A — Vertex Form & Projectile Optimization
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.A — الرأس Form & Projectile Optimization

body.en:
A projectile is launched vertically from an elevated platform. Its height \(h(t)\) in meters after \(t\) seconds is modeled by \(h(t) = -5t^2 + 30t + 35\).
(a) Find the time \(t\) at which the projectile reaches its maximum height, and determine that maximum height.
(b) After how many seconds does the projectile strike the ground?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Maximum Height at Vertex:
    Using \(t_v = -\frac{b}{2a}\) with \(a = -5\) and \(b = 30\):
    \[ t_v = -\frac{30}{2(-5)} = \frac{30}{10} = \mathbf{3\text{ seconds}} \]
    Substitute \(t = 3\) to determine the maximum height:
    \[ h(3) = -5(3)^2 + 30(3) + 35 = -5(9) + 90 + 35 = -45 + 125 = \mathbf{80\text{ meters}} \]
  2. (b) Time to Ground Impact:
    Set \(h(t) = 0\) and solve for positive \(t\):
    \[ -5t^2 + 30t + 35 = 0 \]
    Divide through by \(-5\):
    \[ t^2 - 6t - 7 = 0 \implies (t - 7)(t + 1) = 0 \]
    The roots are \(t = 7\) and \(t = -1\). Rejecting the negative time value gives \(t = \mathbf{7\text{ seconds}}\).
The projectile peaks at 80 meters after 3 seconds and impacts the ground at 7 seconds.

label.en: Worked Example 2.B — Discriminant Analysis & Parameter Determination
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.B — Discriminant Analysis & المعامل Determination

body.en:
For what values of the constant \(k\) does the quadratic equation \(2x^2 - 8x + k = 0\) have:
(a) Exactly one real solution?
(b) Two distinct real solutions?
(c) No real solutions (two complex conjugate solutions)?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. Identify coefficients: \(a = 2\), \(b = -8\), \(c = k\).
  2. Compute the discriminant \(\Delta\):
    \[ \Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-8)^2 - 4(2)(k) = 64 - 8k \]
  3. (a) Exactly One Real Solution:
    Set \(\Delta = 0\):
    \[ 64 - 8k = 0 \implies 8k = 64 \implies \mathbf{k = 8} \]
  4. (b) Two Distinct Real Solutions:
    Set \(\Delta > 0\):
    \[ 64 - 8k > 0 \implies 64 > 8k \implies \mathbf{k < 8} \]
  5. (c) No Real Solutions:
    Set \(\Delta < 0\):
    \[ 64 - 8k < 0 \implies 64 < 8k \implies \mathbf{k > 8} \]
body.ar:
For what values of the الثابت \(k\) does the المعادلة التربيعية \(2x^2 - 8x + k = 0\) have:
(a) Exactly one real الحل?
(b) Two distinct real الحلول?
(c) No real الحلول (two complex conjugate الحلول)?

Step-by-step الحل:
  1. Identify المعاملات: \(a = 2\), \(b = -8\), \(c = k\).
  2. Compute the discriminant \(\Delta\):
    \[ \Delta = b^2 - 4ac = (-8)^2 - 4(2)(k) = 64 - 8k \]
  3. (a) Exactly One Real الحل:
    Set \(\Delta = 0\):
    \[ 64 - 8k = 0 \implies 8k = 64 \implies \mathbf{k = 8} \]
  4. (b) Two Distinct Real الحلول:
    Set \(\Delta > 0\):
    \[ 64 - 8k > 0 \implies 64 > 8k \implies \mathbf{k < 8} \]
  5. (c) No Real الحلول:
    Set \(\Delta < 0\):
    \[ 64 - 8k < 0 \implies 64 < 8k \implies \mathbf{k > 8} \]

label.en: Worked Example 2.C — Vieta's Relations & Polynomial Remainder Theorem
label.ar: مثال محلول 2.C — Vieta's Relations & كثيرة الحدود Remainder مبرهنة

body.en:
(a) Let \(r_1\) and \(r_2\) be the roots of \(3x^2 - 12x + 5 = 0\). Without solving for the individual roots, compute the exact value of \(r_1^2 + r_2^2\).
(b) What is the remainder when \(P(x) = 2x^3 - 5x^2 + 4x - 9\) is divided by \(x - 3\)?

Step-by-step Solution:
  1. (a) Use Vieta's Relations:
    For \(3x^2 - 12x + 5 = 0\), we have:
    \[ r_1 + r_2 = -\frac{-12}{3} = 4, \qquad r_1 r_2 = \frac{5}{3} \]
    Recall the algebraic identity: \((r_1 + r_2)^2 = r_1^2 + 2r_1 r_2 + r_2^2\). Therefore:
    \[ r_1^2 + r_2^2 = (r_1 + r_2)^2 - 2r_1 r_2 = (4)^2 - 2\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) = 16 - \frac{10}{3} = \frac{48 - 10}{3} = \mathbf{\frac{38}{3}} \]
  2. (b) Apply the Remainder Theorem:
    The remainder when \(P(x)\) is divided by \(x - 3\) is \(R = P(3)\):
    \[ P(3) = 2(3)^3 - 5(3)^2 + 4(3) - 9 = 2(27) - 5(9) + 12 - 9 = 54 - 45 + 3 = \mathbf{12} \]
The remainder is \(\mathbf{12}\).

body.en:
Problem (Medium): The graph of the quadratic function \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) is shown below. The parabola intersects the x-axis at points \( (1, 0) \) and \( (p, 0) \), and has a y-intercept of \( (0, -3) \). If the axis of symmetry of the parabola is the line \( x = 2 \), find the value of \( p \).

Step-by-Step Solution: The roots of the quadratic equation \( ax^2 + bx + c = 0 \) are the x-intercepts of the parabola. We are given one root as \( x_1 = 1 \). The axis of symmetry of a parabola given by \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) is \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \). We are given that the axis of symmetry is \( x = 2 \). For a quadratic function, the axis of symmetry is located exactly halfway between the roots. If the roots are \( x_1 \) and \( x_2 \), then the axis of symmetry is \( x = \frac{x_1 + x_2}{2} \). We are given \( x_1 = 1 \) and the axis of symmetry \( x = 2 \). Let the other root be \( p \). Therefore, we have: \[ 2 = \frac{1 + p}{2} \] Multiplying both sides by 2 gives: \[ 4 = 1 + p \] Subtracting 1 from both sides gives: \[ p = 3 \] We can also use the y-intercept to find the value of c. Since the parabola passes through \( (0, -3) \), we have \( y = a(0)^2 + b(0) + c = c \), so \( c = -3 \). The function can be written as \( y = a(x-1)(x-p) \). Substituting \( (0, -3) \) and \( p=3 \), we get: \[ -3 = a(0-1)(0-3) \] \[ -3 = a(-1)(-3) \] \[ -3 = 3a \] \[ a = -1 \] So the quadratic function is \( y = -(x-1)(x-3) = -(x^2 - 4x + 3) = -x^2 + 4x - 3 \). The axis of symmetry is \( x = -\frac{4}{2(-1)} = -\frac{4}{-2} = 2 \), which matches the given information. The roots are \( x=1 \) and \( x=3 \).
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): The التمثيل البياني of the quadratic الدالة \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) is shown below. The القطع المكافئ intersects the x-axis at points \( (1, 0) \) and \( (p, 0) \), and has a y-المقطع of \( (0, -3) \). If the axis of symmetry of the القطع المكافئ is the line \( x = 2 \), أوجد قيمة \( p \).

Step-by-Step الحل: The roots of the المعادلة التربيعية \( ax^2 + bx + c = 0 \) are the x-intercepts of the القطع المكافئ. We are المعطيات one root as \( x_1 = 1 \). The axis of symmetry of a القطع المكافئ المعطيات by \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) is \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \). We are بما أن the axis of symmetry is \( x = 2 \). For a quadratic الدالة, the axis of symmetry is located exactly halfway between the roots. If the roots are \( x_1 \) and \( x_2 \), then the axis of symmetry is \( x = \frac{x_1 + x_2}{2} \). We are المعطيات \( x_1 = 1 \) and the axis of symmetry \( x = 2 \). Let the other root be \( p \). وبالتالي, we have: \[ 2 = \frac{1 + p}{2} \] Multiplying both sides by 2 gives: \[ 4 = 1 + p \] Subtracting 1 from both sides gives: \[ p = 3 \] We can also use the y-المقطع to أوجد قيمة c. Since the القطع المكافئ passes through \( (0, -3) \), we have \( y = a(0)^2 + b(0) + c = c \), so \( c = -3 \). The الدالة can be written as \( y = a(x-1)(x-p) \). Substituting \( (0, -3) \) and \( p=3 \), we get: \[ -3 = a(0-1)(0-3) \] \[ -3 = a(-1)(-3) \] \[ -3 = 3a \] \[ a = -1 \] So the quadratic الدالة is \( y = -(x-1)(x-3) = -(x^2 - 4x + 3) = -x^2 + 4x - 3 \). The axis of symmetry is \( x = -\frac{4}{2(-1)} = -\frac{4}{-2} = 2 \), which matches the المعطيات information. The roots are \( x=1 \) and \( x=3 \).

question.en: Solve the quadratic equation \(3x^2 + 10x - 8 = 0\) by factoring.
question.ar: حل the quadratic equation \(3x^2 + 10x - 8 = 0\) by حلّلing.

solution.en:
Step 1: Find two integers whose product is \(a \cdot c = 3(-8) = -24\) and whose sum is \(b = 10\). The factors are \(+12\) and \(-2\).

Step 2: Split the middle term and factor by grouping: \[ 3x^2 + 12x - 2x - 8 = 0 \implies 3x(x + 4) - 2(x + 4) = 0 \implies (3x - 2)(x + 4) = 0 \]

Step 3: Set each factor to zero: \[ 3x - 2 = 0 \implies x = \frac{2}{3}, \qquad x + 4 = 0 \implies x = -4 \]

The solutions are \(\mathbf{x = \frac{2}{3}}\) and \(\mathbf{x = -4}\).

Step 3: Set each حلّل to zero: \[ 3x - 2 = 0 \implies x = \frac{2}{3}, \qquad x + 4 = 0 \implies x = -4 \]

The solutions are \(\mathbf{x = \frac{2}{3}}\) and \(\mathbf{x = -4}\).

question.en: Convert the quadratic function \(y = 2x^2 - 12x + 11\) into vertex form \(y = a(x - h)^2 + k\). State the coordinates of the vertex and the line of symmetry.
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Quadratics & Polynomials): Convert the quadratic function \(y = 2x^2 - 12x + 11\) into vertex form \(y = a(x - h)^2 + k\). State the coordinates of the vertex and the line of symmetry.

solution.en:
Step 1: Factor the leading coefficient \(a = 2\) from the \(x\)-terms: \[ y = 2(x^2 - 6x) + 11 \]

Step 2: Complete the square inside parentheses. Half of \(-6\) is \(-3\), and \((-3)^2 = 9\): \[ y = 2(x^2 - 6x + 9 - 9) + 11 = 2(x - 3)^2 - 2(9) + 11 = 2(x - 3)^2 - 18 + 11 \]

Step 3: Simplify to vertex form: \[ y = \mathbf{2(x - 3)^2 - 7} \]

The vertex is \(\mathbf{(3, -7)}\) and the axis of symmetry is \(\mathbf{x = 3}\).

question.en: A parabola has its vertex at \((3, -4)\) and passes through the point \((1, 0)\). (a) Write the equation of the parabola in standard form \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\). (b) Determine the coordinates of the other \(x\)-intercept.
question.ar: A parabola has its vertex at \((3, -4)\) and يمر بالنقطة the point \((1, 0)\). (a) Write the equation of the parabola in standard form \(y = ax^2 + bx + c\). (b) حدّد coordinates of the other \(x\)-intercept.

solution.en:
(a) Use vertex form: With vertex \((h, k) = (3, -4)\): \[ y = a(x - 3)^2 - 4 \] Substitute \((x, y) = (1, 0)\) to find \(a\): \[ 0 = a(1 - 3)^2 - 4 \implies 0 = 4a - 4 \implies 4a = 4 \implies a = 1. \] Expand to standard form: \[ y = (x^2 - 6x + 9) - 4 = \mathbf{x^2 - 6x + 5}. \]

(b) Find the other \(x\)-intercept: By symmetry, the \(x\)-intercepts are equidistant from the axis of symmetry \(x = 3\). Since one intercept is at \(x = 1\) (distance \(3 - 1 = 2\)), the other intercept is at \(x = 3 + 2 = 5\), giving \(\mathbf{(5, 0)}\). (Verification: \(x^2 - 6x + 5 = (x - 1)(x - 5) = 0\)).

question.en: If \(x - 2\) is a factor of the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 - kx^2 + 3x - 10\), find the value of \(k\), and determine all real roots of \(P(x)\).
question.ar: إذا كان \(x - 2\) is a حلّل of the polynomial \(P(x) = x^3 - kx^2 + 3x - 10\), أوجد قيمة \(k\), and حدّد all real roots of \(P(x)\).

solution.en:
Step 1: By the Factor Theorem, \(x - 2\) is a factor \(\iff P(2) = 0\): \[ P(2) = (2)^3 - k(2)^2 + 3(2) - 10 = 0 \implies 8 - 4k + 6 - 10 = 0 \implies 4 - 4k = 0 \implies \mathbf{k = 1}. \]

Step 2: Substitute \(k = 1\) into \(P(x) = x^3 - x^2 + 3x - 10\) and divide by \((x - 2)\) using polynomial long division or synthetic division: \[ x^3 - x^2 + 3x - 10 = (x - 2)(x^2 + x + 5). \]

Step 3: Solve \(x^2 + x + 5 = 0\). Its discriminant is \(\Delta = (1)^2 - 4(1)(5) = 1 - 20 = -19 < 0\), which yields no real roots.

Therefore, the value of \(k\) is \(\mathbf{1}\) and the only real root is \(\mathbf{x = 2}\).

question.en: The graph of the quadratic function \( y = x^2 - 6x + 9 \) is a parabola. What is the x-coordinate of the vertex of this parabola?
question.ar: حل المسألة التالية في (Quadratics & Polynomials): The graph of the quadratic function \( y = x^2 - 6x + 9 \) is a parabola. What is the x-coordinate of the vertex of this parabola?

hints.en: The standard form of a quadratic function is \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: The x-coordinate of the vertex of a parabola given in this form is \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \). In the given function, \( y = x^2 - 6x + 9 \), we have \( a = 1 \) and \( b = -6 \).
hints.ar: تلميح للحل: استخدم العلاقة \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \) ، \( y = x^2 - 6x + 9 \) ، \( a = 1 \) ، \( b = -6 \) لتبسيط الخطوة.

hints.en: Therefore, the x-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(1)}\).
hints.ar: وبالتالي، the x-coordinate of the vertex is \(x = -\frac{-6}{2(1)}\).

solution.en: The standard form of a quadratic function is \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \). The x-coordinate of the vertex of a parabola given in this form is \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \). In the given function, \( y = x^2 - 6x + 9 \), we have \( a = 1 \) and \( b = -6 \). Therefore, the x-coordinate of the vertex is \( x = -\frac{-6}{2(1)} = -\frac{-6}{2} = 3 \).
solution.ar: The standard form of a quadratic function is \( y = ax^2 + bx + c \). The x-coordinate of the vertex of a parabola given in this form is \( x = -\frac{b}{2a} \). In the given function, \( y = x^2 - 6x + 9 \), we have \( a = 1 \) and \( b = -6 \). وبالتالي، the x-coordinate of the vertex is \( x = -\frac{-6}{2(1)} = -\frac{-6}{2} = 3 \).

label.en: ● Master Atlas of the 9 Main Parent Functions & Universal Transformation Law
label.ar: ● الأطلس الشامل للدوال الأم التسع وقانون التحويلات الهندسية العام

body.en:
Every algebraic and elementary transcendental model is built by transforming one of the nine core parent functions via \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\), where \(|a|\) scales vertically (reflecting across the \(x\)-axis if \(a < 0\)), \(h\) shifts horizontally, and \(k\) shifts vertically:

FamilyTransformed Form \(g(x)\)DomainRange (\(a > 0\))Key Geometric Feature
Constant\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)Horizontal line, slope \(0\)
Linear\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Constant slope \(m = a\), pivot \((h, k)\)
Quadratic\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Parabola vertex \((h, k)\), axis \(x = h\)
Cubic\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Inflection center \((h, k)\), S-curve
Absolute Value\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)V-corner vertex \((h, k)\), slopes \(\pm a\)
Radical\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)Endpoint \((h, k)\), half-parabola
Rational\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), horizontal \(y = k\)
Exponential\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)Horizontal asymptote \(y = k\), anchor \((h, a+k)\)
Logarithmic\(a\ln(x - h) + k\)\((h, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)Vertical asymptote \(x = h\), anchor \((h+1, k)\)
body.ar:
تُبنى النماذج الجبرية والمتسامية الأساسية من خلال تطبيق التحويل القياسي \(g(x) = a\,f(x - h) + k\) على إحدى الدوال الأم التسع، حيث يتحكم \(|a|\) في التمدد الرأسي (مع انعكاس حول محور السينات إذا كان \(a < 0\))، ويمثل \(h\) الإزاحة الأفقية، و\(k\) الإزاحة الرأسية:

عائلة الدالةالصورة المحوّلة \(g(x)\)المجالالمدى (\(a > 0\))السمة الهندسية المميزة
الثابتة\(f(x) = c\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\(\{c\}\)مستقيم أفقي ميله \(0\)
الخطية\(a(x - h) + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)ميل ثابت \(m = a\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, k)\)
التربيعية\(a(x - h)^2 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)قطع مكافئ رأسه \((h, k)\) ومحوره \(x = h\)
التكعيبية\(a(x - h)^3 + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)نقطة انعطاف مركزية \((h, k)\)
القيمة المطلقة\(a|x - h| + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)رأس زاوي على شكل V عند \((h, k)\) بميلين \(\pm a\)
الجذرية\(a\sqrt{x - h} + k\)\([h, \infty)\)\([k, \infty)\)نقطة بداية \((h, k)\) ومجال مقيّد \(x \ge h\)
النسبية (المقلوب)\(\dfrac{a}{x - h} + k\)\(x \neq h\)\(y \neq k\)تقارب رأسي \(x = h\) وتقارب أفقي \(y = k\)
الأسية\(a \cdot 2^{x - h} + k\)\((-\infty, \infty)\)\((k, \infty)\)تقارب أفقي \(y = k\) ونقطة ارتكاز \((h, a+k)\)
